processing: As with jasmine teas generally, a green tea base is layered with fresh jasmine blossoms so it absorbs their scent, and the spent flowers are then sieved out; better lots repeat this several times.
harvest_season: Typical of jasmine tea, the base is picked in spring and scented when jasmine blooms in summer; dates for this tea are not recorded.
appearance_dry: Typical of jasmine tea, dark green twisted leaf, perhaps with a few pale dried petals.
appearance_liquor: Typical of jasmine green tea, clear pale yellow-green.
appearance_wet: Typical of the class, soft green leaf with a strong floral smell.
taste_profile: Described only by class: jasmine perfume over a light green tea base, sweet and floral, with little bitterness when brewed cool.

brewing.notes: General advice for jasmine green tea: water below the boil and moderate steeps, because hot water and long steeps bring out bitterness from the base.

vintage_note: Usual for scented green tea: sold by the current year's scenting and best drunk within a year or so, as the jasmine fades with time. There is no ageing market.
description:
Guangzhou jasmine tea appears on lists of Guangdong's flower teas, alongside rose black tea and chrysanthemum pu-erh. Beyond the name and the place, little is documented about this particular tea.

As with other jasmine teas, the character comes from scenting: green tea and fresh blossoms lie together, the leaf takes on the perfume, and the flowers are removed. The number of scentings usually tells you more than the name does.

Expect what is typical of the class, a light green base under sweet jasmine. Keep the water under the boil, and shorten the steeps if bitterness shows.

When buying, ask how many times the tea was scented and with what, and be wary of anything that smells of perfume rather than flowers. Guangxi's Hengzhou and Fujian's Fuzhou are the better known jasmine regions if you want a point of comparison.
history: Little is documented about this tea's origins. It is recorded in surveys of Guangdong's notable teas as one of the province's flower teas, without dates or named makers.
